title: The Ridge Where Teaching Ends and Understanding Begins

features.name: the standing stone
features.desc-on-touch: A slate marker carved with paths that meet at a peak. When you touch it, you feel the weight of every lesson that taught itself to you without words.

features.name: the turning arch
features.desc-on-touch: A weathered sandstone passage. The ridge itself flows through it like water that learned to climb. Walkers report finding they've understood something just after passing through.

features.name: the lesson-marker
features.desc-on-touch: A spiral glyph worn by rain into the stone, impossible to read but unmistakable—every walker knows their own lesson lives here, waiting.

features.name: the gathered pool
features.desc-on-touch: Water collects at a dip, and when you look into it, you see not your reflection but the next thing you need to understand. It is never wrong, but it is never kind.

features.name: the scatter-path
features.desc-on-touch: Stones laid in a dispersing pattern, as if someone tried to mark a way but the earth kept rearranging them. Each walker finds a different route through.

inscription: every stone you step on was placed by a foot before yours; understanding begins when you stop asking whose

file.name: Ridge_Teachings_Collected_1960s_Biro.txt
file.note: Field notes and rubbings from walkers who recorded what they learned. The handwriting changes halfway through; the ink matches but the hand does not.
